PullRequest.Title: agentHost: remove compact artifact prompt experiment
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- remove the `chat.artifactTools.compactPrompts` experiment and Agent Host configuration plumbing
- keep the full artifact registration guidance introduced by #335631 as the only prompt format
- preserve Add tool eagerness and List/Remove deferral and discovery behavior
- simplify related tests to cover the single prompt format

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- verified no compact-prompt setting, schema key, selection helper, or experiment references remain
- transpilation and unit tests were not run because `npm` is unavailable in the current environment (`npm: command not found`)

Scenarios.Scenario: First user turn in a new Agent Host chat with artifact tools enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Contribution collection runs before agent.chats.sendMessage; the artifact instruction is added to hostInstructions and therefore reaches the provider request critical path. The existing memento limits this instruction to the first turn of each chat.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the user turn, host instructions, and tool metadata to the selected model provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider send per user turn; the changed artifact instruction is included only on the first turn of each chat. The enabled Add tool remains one tool definition, with List and Remove still deferred where provider support exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single provider send occurred. Depending on the experiment assignment, it carried either compact or original artifact wording; the PR standardizes on the original wording.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The provider send is the turn's critical path. Former compact-treatment users receive a fixed larger instruction and schema, but the diff does not add a request or increase request count with artifacts, sessions, or history.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of newly created chats controls how often the first-turn instruction is sent; within one chat it does not scale with turn count. Tool count and artifact collection size are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new parallelism or burst is introduced. Contribution processing remains serial and each turn performs the existing single provider dispatch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The per-chat firstTurnSeen memento is the effective cache and suppresses the instruction after the first turn, including hydrated non-empty chats. No cache key, invalidation, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the full wording reaches the first provider request and that the memento bounds it to once per chat; high confidence that request cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact tokenization and provider latency impact of replacing compact wording with the full wording varies by provider/model, but the increase is a small constant rather than input-scaled or repeated per turn.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The fixed prompt-size increase is intentional, bounded, and does not establish meaningful latency, throughput, CPU, memory, or network degradation under realistic scaling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent session startup and server-tool registration for Copilot, Claude, and Codex
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each provider obtains the session's server-tool definitions while materializing the session/thread. Copilot maps definitions to SDK tools, Claude builds one in-process MCP server, and Codex builds dynamic tool specs before the session can use those tools.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Convert enabled server-tool definitions into Copilot SDK tool registrations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One conversion per enabled tool during session setup; artifact tool membership remains three definitions and only wording selection was removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same definitions were converted, with the schema selected from compact or original wording.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session setup performs the same bounded mapping as before, now without a configuration-dependent definition selector.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct an in-process Claude MCP tool for each server-tool definition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One construction per enabled definition; artifact definitions remain Add, List, and Remove, with unchanged always-load/deferred flags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same three artifact tools were constructed using one of two wording variants.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is part of Claude startup wiring, but the diff neither adds tools nor adds SDK calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Include server tools in Codex thread/start dynamic tool specifications sent to the Codex process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One spec per unique enabled tool at thread start; deduplication and artifact tool count are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same thread/start registration occurred with compact or original schema wording according to configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Thread startup carries a fixed schema-size difference for former compact users, with no extra IPC operation or per-item fan-out.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled server-tool count controls setup work; this PR does not change effective cardinality. Session count controls repetitions exactly as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Claude still constructs definitions through one bounded Promise.all over enabled tools; Copilot and Codex map synchronously. The diff adds no cross-session or per-tool concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Definitions are static after the change rather than selected on each lookup from configuration. Session materialization and deferred-tool behavior are unchanged; there is no new cache or miss path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from all three provider call paths and tests asserting unchanged deferral/eagerness.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider SDK internals may serialize schemas differently, but all observed registration counts and eager/deferred flags are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Static definitions remove configuration reads and alternate-definition allocation; the bounded wording increase does not alter tool cardinality, boundary count, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add, list, or remove session artifacts and persist artifact state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A model invokes an existing server tool; Add/Remove mutate SessionArtifacts and call the accessor's existing persistence function, while List only reads current session state. Prompt selection is not consulted during execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the ordered visible session artifact list so it survives host restart.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one persistence operation per Add or successful Remove invocation, with related Add entries still batched in one call; List performs no persistence. Cardinality is unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical persistence callback and batching behavior ran; useCompactPrompts only selected metadata and was never part of artifact mutation or persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence remains awaited by the tool execution path and therefore can affect tool completion, but no boundary operation was introduced or moved.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tool invocations and artifacts batched per Add call control work. Neither collection processing nor effective persistence cardinality changed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing mutation serialization/ordering is unchanged; removing the prompt accessor does not alter concurrent Add/Remove behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SessionArtifacts read/mutate behavior and centrally persisted state are unchanged. Restart listing still avoids local database reads as covered by the retained tests.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the unchanged execute implementation and accessor diff, which removes only useCompactPrompts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Persistence duration depends on session storage, but the diff has no causal effect on its frequency or payload.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression because artifact execution, batching, persistence boundaries, and lifecycle are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench-to-Agent-Host configuration synchronization and startup schema construction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration properties and the root protocol schema are built/serialized for Agent Host configuration sync. The compact-prompts setting and root key are removed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward configured Agent Host values from the renderer to the Agent Host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fewer configuration entry can be synchronized; no new entry or message is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Configuration sync could include the compact-prompts boolean independently of artifact-tool enablement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Any configuration-sync payload is marginally smaller, so the diff does not add startup or update work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of synchronized configuration properties; this PR decreases it by one constant entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configuration synchronization scheduling is unchanged and no new asynchronous operation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. The removed setting no longer requires reading or forwarding; artifact-tool enablement remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from removal of the setting, schema property, accessor read, and synchronization tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The saving is negligible, but there is no plausible degradation mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance issue; work and serialized configuration state are reduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 16 changed files and all diff pages. Traced first-turn prompt injection, provider tool registration across Copilot/Claude/Codex, artifact persistence, and configuration sync. The PR standardizes bounded wording while preserving request/tool/persistence cardinality, deferral, concurrency, and lifecycle; no actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
